learn.title: Three small puzzles
learn.body: Time to combine what you know: variables, operators, loops and functions. Each puzzle below is small. Read the plan, predict the result, and then try writing your own version before checking.

learn.title: Challenge 1: a pyramid
learn.body: Row r has `h - r` spaces and then `2 * r - 1` hashes. For h = 3:

learn.title: How it works
learn.body: The outer loop picks the row. The first inner loop prints the spaces that push the pyramid to the middle. The second prints an odd count of hashes: 1, 3 and 5. A new line then ends the row. Change `h` to make it taller.

learn.title: Row 2 by hand
steps: The space loop runs from `s = 2` up to 2, so once: one space
The hash loop runs `k` from 1 to 3, so three hashes
Row 2 is a space and ###, which is centred under row 1

learn.title: Challenge 2: fewest coins
learn.body: Make 87 cents from 25, 10, 5 and 1. Take as many big coins as possible first.

learn.title: Greedy change
learn.body: 87 gives 3 quarters (75), leaving 12. That is 1 dime, leaving 2, then 0 nickels and 2 pennies. Total 3 + 1 + 2 is 6 coins. Taking the biggest coin first works for these coins. For other coin sets it can fail: for 6 with coins 4, 3 and 1, greedy uses 3 coins but 3 + 3 uses only 2.

learn.title: Challenge 3: a checksum
learn.body: A check digit helps catch typing mistakes. Add all the digits of a number.

learn.title: The checksum idea
learn.body: The digits of 4729 add up to 22. Choose a check digit so the total becomes a multiple of 10: the next digit is 8, giving 47298. Its digit sum is 30, and `30 % 10` is 0. If someone mistypes one digit, the total is no longer a multiple of 10, so the error is caught.
Real card numbers use a stronger scheme called Luhn's algorithm. This simple sum misses swapped digits, since 4279 has the same digit sum as 4729.

questions.prompt: The pyramid with h = 3 prints how many hash symbols on its last row? Type the number.
How many spaces start row 1 of the h = 3 pyramid? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Row 1 has `h - r`, which is 3 - 1, so 2 spaces.

questions.prompt: Fewest coins for 87 cents using 25, 10, 5 and 1. Type the number of coins.
questions.explanation: 3 quarters, 1 dime and 2 pennies make 6 coins.

questions.prompt: With coins 4, 3 and 1, the fewest coins for 6 is what?
questions.explanation: Greedy picks 4, 1, 1 for 3 coins, but 3 + 3 uses only 2. Greedy is not always best.

questions.prompt: What is the digit sum of 4729? Type the number.
What check digit makes 4729 plus a digit sum to a multiple of 10?
Why does the simple digit-sum checksum miss swapped digits?
choices: A swap keeps the same total
It only checks the last digit
questions.explanation: 4729 and 4279 have the same digits, so the same sum.

questions.prompt: In `n % 10`, `n / 10` digit loops, which line removes the last digit?
questions.explanation: Integer division by 10 drops the last digit.
